Add a CI gate for pull request texts (#268)

Add tools/check-pr-text.py, a gate that checks a pull request
description and its committed squash-message file,
.github/squash/<number>.txt. In both texts it checks review-history
labels, through the label lint loaded by file path, em and en dashes,
-ise spellings, an empty or blank text and a code fence that is never
closed; in the squash message it also checks line width, revision ids
and a subject that ends with the pull request number. The gate's
docstring states each rule, the masks and exemptions, and the exit
contract with its precondition. Add its suite,
tools/test-check-pr-text.py, with a failing case for each defect
class, cases at the edges of each mask and exemption, and a mutant
sweep whose sites are generated from the gate source, and the
workflow .github/workflows/pr-text.yml, which runs the suite and the
gate on every pull request with read-only permissions, keeps no
credentials after checkout and stops the job after 10 minutes.
tools/ci-status.py does not insist on the new check.
tools/run_all_checks.sh runs the gate's suite, and
tools/test-run-all-checks.py lists the workflow's event step as an
exception, with the suite in its place.

Residuals: a defect in a form the patterns miss, such as an upper-case
revision id or an -ise stem the denylist lacks; a defect inside a
masked region, or in a region the gate masks but a renderer shows as
prose, such as text glued after a URL by a comma; a false failure on
honest text that the gate reads otherwise than a renderer shows it,
such as code in an indented block; a run outside the precondition of
the exit contract, such as a label lint that ends the gate process or
replaces its standard output; a message typed into the merge dialog
that differs from the committed file; a description edited after the
last run; and a change to the gate outside the operators of the
sweep, such as a change of 2 tokens at once.
